tools.name: k8s_cluster_health
tools.description: Pod health across the WHOLE cluster in one call: scans every namespace and returns only what is wrong (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled, Pending, not-ready) plus per-phase counts and how many pods/namespaces were actually scanned. USE THIS FIRST for any cluster-wide question — 'is anything broken', 'status check', 'cluster health', 'any pods down'. k8s_list_pods only sees ONE namespace, so answering those questions with it gives a partial answer that reads like a complete one. Pass namespace ONLY to narrow to a single namespace; omit it for the whole cluster. If scanned.complete is false the scan hit its ceiling — say so instead of reporting all-clear.

namespace.description: Optional — omit to scan the entire cluster (no default namespace)

restart_window_minutes.description: How recent a restart still counts as flapping for a now-ready pod (default: 60)

tools.name: k8s_correlate_pods
tools.description: Do several broken pods share ONE cause? Diffs the failing pods against the HEALTHY pods in the same namespace and returns what the broken set shares that no healthy pod has — node, image, ConfigMap, Secret, PVC, ServiceAccount, env variable names. USE THIS whenever more than one pod is failing, BEFORE investigating them one by one: k8s_describe_pod on each and comparing the specs yourself is what turns one shared root cause into eight separate write-ups. Omit `pods` to take every not-ready pod in the namespace (the natural follow-up to k8s_cluster_health). Read `uniqueToBroken` FIRST — `sharedWithHealthy` is mostly noise, because pods of one Deployment share nearly everything. An empty `uniqueToBroken` is a real answer: it says a single shared cause is unlikely, so look at the node, a recent deploy, or an upstream dependency instead. The output is a LEAD, never a conclusion — confirm the shared attribute with its own tool call before naming it as the root cause.

pods.description: Pod names to treat as broken (default: every not-ready pod in the namespace)

label_selector.description: Optional label selector to narrow which pods are considered at all

tools.name: k8s_list_namespaces
tools.description: List all namespaces in the Kubernetes cluster

tools.name: k8s_list_nodes
tools.description: List all nodes with status, roles, and resource capacity

tools.name: k8s_list_pods
tools.description: List pods in ONE namespace. For 'is anything broken across the cluster' use k8s_cluster_health instead — this tool cannot see past a single namespace

tools.name: k8s_get_pod_logs
tools.description: Get logs from a pod container. Set `previous: true` to read the CRASHED/prior container instance (the current logs are the fresh restart — CrashLoop root cause is in the previous one). `since_seconds` limits to a recent window.

previous.description: Logs from the previous (crashed) container instance (default: false)

container.description: Container name. Optional: on a pod with several containers (a sidecar, a proxy, a log shipper) omit it and the tool reads the one that is failing — restarted, or not ready — and names it and the others in the result, so you can ask for a different one by name.

since_seconds.description: Only logs from the last N seconds (optional)

tools.name: k8s_describe_pod
tools.description: Detailed status of ONE pod (the 'describe' view): per-container state incl. the exact termination/waiting reason (OOMKilled, exit code, CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff), restart counts, pod conditions, QoS, configured requests/limits, node. Use this for crash/OOM/not-Ready RCA — it gives the ground-truth reason logs only hint at. (No CPU/mem usage — that's Prometheus.) For a pod stuck Terminating it also returns `deletionTimestamp`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` and `finalizers` — those three decide the cause, and they are absent on a pod that is not being deleted.

tools.name: k8s_describe_node
tools.description: Detailed status of ONE node: conditions (Ready, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure), taints, unschedulable flag, capacity vs allocatable, kubelet/OS version. Use for Pending pods / node-level incidents. (No live usage — that's Prometheus.)

tools.name: k8s_get_endpoints
tools.description: Ready vs not-ready backend addresses (pods) behind a Service — answers 'does this Service have any ready endpoints?'. readyCount=0 explains 503 / connection-refused when the Service exists but has no healthy pods. Pass the Service name.

tools.name: k8s_list_deployments
tools.description: List deployments in a namespace, including each container's name and image (use this to answer image/tag questions)

tools.name: k8s_list_statefulsets
tools.description: List StatefulSets in a namespace, including each container's name and image

tools.name: k8s_list_daemonsets
tools.description: List DaemonSets in a namespace, including each container's name and image

tools.name: k8s_get_rollout_status
tools.description: Rollout progress of ONE Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet: desired vs updated/ready/available/unavailable replicas, `complete` flag, and conditions (e.g. Progressing=False ProgressDeadlineExceeded). Use for 'deploy stuck / not rolling out'.

tools.name: k8s_list_replicasets
tools.description: List ReplicaSets in a namespace with owner Deployment + revision + desired/ready + each container's image — rollout history (which RS is active vs stale, failed old RS). The image a rollback should go back to is the `images` entry of the newest older revision that still has ready pods: read it here rather than guessing a tag.

tools.name: k8s_list_pvs
tools.description: List PersistentVolumes (cluster-scoped): phase (Bound/Available/Released/Failed), capacity, storageClass, reclaimPolicy, bound claim — for storage incidents

tools.name: k8s_list_storageclasses
tools.description: List StorageClasses: provisioner, default flag, reclaim/binding mode — a PVC stuck Pending often means no default class or a broken provisioner

tools.name: k8s_list_network_policies
tools.description: List NetworkPolicies in a namespace: podSelector, policyTypes, rule counts — for 'traffic blocked' investigations (a deny-all policy or missing allow rule)

tools.name: k8s_list_pdbs
tools.description: List PodDisruptionBudgets in a namespace: min/maxUnavailable + disruptionsAllowed — disruptionsAllowed=0 blocks node drain/eviction and can stall rollouts

tools.name: k8s_get_sa_permissions
tools.description: What a ServiceAccount is allowed to do: its Role/ClusterRole bindings and the resolved rules (apiGroups/resources/verbs). Use for `forbidden` / permission-denied RCA — shows whether the SA is missing a needed permission.

tools.name: k8s_list_jobs
tools.description: List Jobs in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_cronjobs
tools.description: List CronJobs in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_services
tools.description: List Services in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_ingresses
tools.description: List Ingresses in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_hpas
tools.description: List HorizontalPodAutoscalers in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_pvcs
tools.description: List PersistentVolumeClaims in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_resource_quotas
tools.description: List ResourceQuotas in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_events
tools.description: List events in a namespace, optionally filtered by time

since_minutes.description: Only return events from the last N minutes (optional)

tools.name: k8s_list_crds
tools.description: List all CustomResourceDefinitions in the cluster (the types — use k8s_get_custom_resources for the objects)

tools.name: k8s_get_custom_resources
tools.description: Read custom resource OBJECTS of any CRD — e.g. Flux HelmRelease/Kustomization, cert-manager Certificate. Without `name`: compact list (name + Ready condition + message). With `name`: the full object (spec + status). Find group/version/plural via k8s_list_crds if unsure.

tools.name: k8s_find_by_name
tools.description: Find every object with this EXACT name across the kinds people name things by — Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, CronJob, Job, Pod, Service, Ingress, ConfigMap, Secret (name only), ServiceAccount, PersistentVolumeClaim — in one namespace or in all. Use it when you do not know what KIND a named object is, and before concluding that something does not exist: a lookup by a guessed kind comes back empty and reads exactly like absence. It says what a name IS, not whether it is unused — for a cleanup, k8s_find_unused_resources is still required. A name that is a namespace is reported as one. Each match carries its namespace and managedBy (flux / helm / none). Exact names only — it never suggests similar ones.

namespace.description: Namespace to search — omit to search every namespace

tools.name: k8s_get_resource
tools.description: Get ANY Kubernetes resource by apiVersion + kind — the full object (spec + status) when `name` is given, or a compact list when it's omitted. Works for built-ins (apiVersion `v1`, `apps/v1`, `batch/v1`, `networking.k8s.io/v1`, …) AND custom resources. Use when there's no dedicated tool for the kind, or you need the raw object. Discover which apiVersions this cluster serves via k8s_list_api_resources.

tools.name: k8s_list_api_resources
tools.description: Discover which API groups/versions this cluster serves (like `kubectl api-resources`/`api-versions`): core v1 kinds + every group with its versions. Use to find the right apiVersion for k8s_get_resource. For CRD types and their plurals use k8s_list_crds.

tools.name: k8s_list_service_accounts
tools.description: List ServiceAccounts in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_configmaps
tools.description: List ConfigMaps in a namespace with their keys and data

tools.name: k8s_list_secrets
tools.description: List Secrets in a namespace (name and type only, values are not exposed)

tools.name: prometheus_query
tools.description: Execute an instant PromQL query

tools.name: prometheus_query_range
tools.description: Execute a range PromQL query

tools.name: prometheus_get_targets
tools.description: Get scrape targets and their health status

tools.name: prometheus_get_rules
tools.description: Get all alerting and recording rules

tools.name: prometheus_get_metadata
tools.description: Get metric metadata (type, unit, help text)

tools.name: prometheus_list_metric_names
tools.description: List all available metric names

tools.name: alertmanager_get_alerts
tools.description: Get every alert Alertmanager is currently holding, in Alertmanager's own groups. This is the cluster-wide view of what is firing across ALL alert sources (Prometheus rules, log-based rules, anything else routed here) — use it to establish blast radius: is this incident isolated, or one symptom of something larger? Each alert is labelled with its status: active, silenced (a human muted the notification — the problem is still firing), or inhibited (suppressed by a higher-severity alert). Returns a summary with complete counts plus per-group detail.

filter.description: Optional label matchers, Alertmanager syntax, e.g. ['namespace="payments"'] or ['severity=~"critical|warning"']. Omit to see the whole cluster — which is what blast radius needs.

tools.name: loki_query
tools.description: Execute an instant LogQL query against Loki

tools.name: loki_query_range
tools.description: Query logs over a time range from Loki

tools.name: loki_get_labels
tools.description: Get all label names available in Loki

tools.name: loki_get_label_values
tools.description: Get values for a specific label in Loki

tools.name: loki_get_streams
tools.description: List active log streams matching a label selector

tools.name: loki_get_stats
tools.description: Get ingestion statistics for a log stream (bytes, lines, chunks)

tools.name: tracing_search
tools.description: Search distributed traces (Tempo/Jaeger). Find slow or failing requests by service, minimum duration, and time window. Returns trace summaries — use tracing_get_trace for span detail.

end.description: Window end — RFC3339 or Unix seconds (default: now)

start.description: Window start — RFC3339 or Unix seconds (default: 1h ago)

service.description: Service name to filter by (REQUIRED for Jaeger backend, optional for Tempo)

minDurationMs.description: Only traces slower than this many milliseconds

tools.name: tracing_get_trace
tools.description: Get the full span tree for one trace by ID. Returns normalized spans (service, name, durationMs, parent, error) to pinpoint which span/service is slow or failing.

tools.name: tracing_list_services
tools.description: List service names known to the tracing backend (discovery before searching).

tools.name: k8s_find_unused_resources
tools.description: Orphaned/idle Kubernetes objects across the cluster in ONE call (the `kor` question): PVCs nothing mounts, Services with zero endpoint addresses, Deployments/StatefulSets scaled to 0, DaemonSets that match no node, and ConfigMaps/Secrets/ServiceAccounts nothing references. USE THIS for 'what can we clean up', 'unused resources', 'orphaned', 'idle', 'wasted', 'cost'. References are read from running pods AND every workload pod template, so a scaled-to-zero Deployment does NOT make its config look unused. Two more filters run on top: an object with an ownerReference is left out (its controller owns its lifecycle), and every surviving ConfigMap/Secret/PVC/ServiceAccount is cross-checked against EVERY custom resource in the cluster — so a ConfigMap an operator names in its CR spec is removed from the list, and `crossCheck.suppressed` says which CR saved it. ALWAYS read `crossCheck` and `note` before reporting: `crdsUnreadable` is non-empty when RBAC blocked some CRDs, and then the cross-check was PARTIAL — say so instead of calling the list verified. It stays a REVIEW list, not a delete list: an object read by name at runtime leaves no trace anywhere. Never propose deleting one without naming its owner. For sizing (requests/limits vs real usage) use k8s_recommend_resources instead — this tool reads no metrics.

namespace.description: Optional — omit to scan the whole cluster

cross_check_crds.description: Cross-check candidates against every custom resource in the cluster (default: true). Turn off only if the scan is too slow — the result is then unverified against operators

include_system_namespaces.description: Include kube-* namespaces (default: false — they are full of managed objects that only look unused)

tools.name: k8s_recommend_resources
tools.description: Right-sizing: compares each container's CONFIGURED requests/limits against its REAL usage from Prometheus and returns per-container recommendations plus the cluster's over-reserved CPU/memory. USE THIS for 'resource limits', 'requests', 'right-size', 'over-provisioned', 'how much does X actually use', and as the Short-term action in any OOMKilled / CPU-throttling / Pending-pod RCA — it produces the concrete number to change, so the recommendation is `512Mi -> 900Mi`, not 'consider raising the limit'. Flags: `oom_risk`, `cpu_throttled`, `cpu_under_provisioned`, `memory_under_provisioned`, `no_requests`, `over_provisioned`, `no_data`. Read `method` before quoting a number — it is a percentile heuristic over `window`, not a VPA verdict. Do NOT use it to find orphaned objects; that is k8s_find_unused_resources.

window.description: Lookback for the usage stats, e.g. 6h, 24h, 7d (default: 24h)

workload.description: Optional Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet name to narrow to

namespace.description: Optional — omit for every non-kube-* namespace

tools.name: k8s_rollout_restart
tools.description: [WRITE] Rolling-restart a Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet (kubectl rollout restart equivalent). Only works in namespaces listed in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. Call with dry_run=true first to validate the target without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

tools.name: k8s_set_image
tools.description: [WRITE] Change one container's image on a Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet (e.g. fix a nonexistent/broken image tag). Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates and reports current → new image without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

container.description: Container name within the pod template. Optional — omit for single-container workloads (auto-resolved)

tools.name: k8s_set_resources
tools.description: [WRITE] Update one container's resource requests/limits on a Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet (e.g. raise the memory limit after OOMKilled). Only provided values are changed. Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

container.description: Container name within the pod template. Optional — omit for single-container workloads (auto-resolved)

tools.name: k8s_scale
tools.description: [WRITE] Change the replica count of a Deployment/StatefulSet (DaemonSets have no replicas). Bounded by MAX_SCALE_DELTA. Scaling to zero is refused unless quarantine=true, which is only for a workload k8s_recommend_resources listed under idleWorkloads — a reversible alternative to deleting something that looks unused. Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

replicas.description: Target replica count (>= 1, or 0 with quarantine=true)

quarantine.description: Allow replicas=0 as a reversible quarantine of a workload measured idle over >=24h. Undo by scaling back to the original count. Never set this to retire a workload you have not measured.

tools.name: k8s_delete_pod
tools.description: [WRITE] Delete ONE stuck/wedged pod so its controller recreates it fresh (same spec). Refused for pods without a recreating controller (ReplicaSet/StatefulSet/DaemonSet) — no replacement = outage. GitOps-safe (like rollout_restart). Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates the target and reports the owning controller without changing anything.

pod.description: Exact pod name (not the workload name)

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

tools.name: k8s_delete_orphan
tools.description: [WRITE] Delete ONE abandoned object that nothing declares — a ConfigMap, Service, ServiceAccount, or a Deployment/StatefulSet already at 0 replicas. Only for objects k8s_find_unused_resources listed under `orphanKeys` (managedBy: none). REFUSED when anything declares it (Flux/Helm — remove it from the GitOps repo instead), when an ownerReference explains it, or when a workload still runs replicas. There is no minimum age on this server right now, so do not refuse one for being new — but state how old it is, because age is the only evidence of abandonment there is. Secrets and PersistentVolumeClaims are NOT supported and never will be: a Secret's backup is its credentials and a PVC's manifest is not its data. Returns `backupManifest` — the object as `kubectl apply` takes it back, captured immediately before deletion. That is the entire undo, so store it. Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true returns the manifest and every refusal without deleting anything.

kind.description: Object kind. No secret, no persistentvolumeclaim — neither can be restored from a manifest.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

tools.name: flux_reconcile
tools.description: [WRITE] Force Flux to re-apply the GitOps repo's declared state for a workload's HelmRelease (flux reconcile helmrelease --force equivalent), reverting changes made directly in the cluster. Use when the cluster has DRIFTED from Git (someone patched it outside GitOps) — it restores the declared state, it never introduces a new one. Refused for workloads not managed by a Flux HelmRelease. Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

*🟡 Severity:* Medium

*⚡ TL;DR*
- The storefront service is emitting downstream-timeout errors to checkout-gateway, and its readiness probe is repeatedly failing (HTTP 503), suggesting the downstream dependency is slow or blocked.
- Immediate action: scale checkout-gateway to 2 replicas to absorb downstream load and reduce the downstream timeout pressure.

*⚠️ Impact if Unresolved*
- Downstream timeouts can propagate to storefront requests, causing higher latency and potential 5xx backpressure to upstream clients. If storefront remains not-ready due to downstream failures, user requests may see increased latency or errors and end-to-end throughput could deteriorate. The blast radius appears limited to storefront->checkout-gateway and its direct consumers, but the exact upstream impact depends on traffic patterns and any retry behavior.

*🔧 Recommended Actions*
1. *Immediate:* scale `checkout-gateway` to 2 replicas in namespace `sample-apps`.
2. *Short-term:* monitor storefront readiness, checkout-gateway throughput, and downstream latency; consider temporarily increasing checkout-gateway CPU/memory if saturation is observed.
3. *Long-term:* add resilience for the gateway path (circuit breaker, timeout tuning, connection pool sizing) and verify readiness path stability; ensure endpoints behind checkout-gateway have adequate capacity and health checks.

*🧭 Runbook*
1. *Verify:* confirm downstream timeouts from storefront to checkout-gateway and readiness health of storefront under load.
```
kubectl get deploy checkout-gateway -n sample-apps
kubectl get deploy storefront -n sample-apps
```
2. *Fix:* scale checkout-gateway to 2 replicas in namespace sample-apps.
3. *Confirm:* verify storefront can serve requests with reduced downstream latency and storefront readiness remains healthy.
```
kubectl get deploy checkout-gateway -n sample-apps
kubectl get deploy storefront -n sample-apps
```

*📍 Root Cause*
1. *Symptom:* AppErrorLogSpike in storefront indicating downstream timeouts to checkout-gateway — _log-alert_ `sample-apps/storefront/storefront-7ff755c7dd-kpl8z`
2. *Because:* DownstreamError: checkout-gateway timed out after 50ms observed in storefront logs — _Loki_ `sample-apps/storefront/storefront-7ff755c7dd-kpl8z`
3. *Because:* Readiness probe failed with HTTP 503 on the storefront pod, implying the service was not ready to serve while downstream timeouts occurred — _Kubernetes events_ for `sample-apps/storefront/storefront-7ff755c7dd-kpl8z`
4. *Because:* The storefront container previously terminated (lastState) with exit 255, indicating a prior abnormal termination that could contribute to instability or readiness flakiness — _Kubernetes pod describe_ `sample-apps/storefront/storefront-7ff755c7dd-kpl8z`
⛔ *Not visible from here:* The exact current endpoint readiness for the checkout-gateway Service (ready endpoints vs. zero) and real-time traffic shaping between storefront and checkout-gateway are not visible from the current snapshot; would require k8s_get_endpoints and a live PromQL window during peak load.

*📊 Evidence*
• *Fact:* The Loki log stream for `sample-apps/storefront/storefront-7ff755c7dd-kpl8z` shows repeated DownstreamError: checkout-gateway timed out after 50ms and gateway call failed messages — evidence of downstream latency impacting storefront — _Loki_ `sample-apps/storefront/storefront-7ff755c7dd-kpl8z`  
• *Fact:* Storefront readiness events show Readiness probe failed: HTTP 503 repeated, indicating storefront is not ready under current downstream pressure — _Kubernetes events_ for `sample-apps/storefront/storefront-7ff755c7dd-kpl8z`  
• *Fact:* Pod describe data shows storefront container with lastState Terminated: Unknown (exit 255) on a prior instance, suggesting residual instability that could affect readiness — _Kubernetes pod describe_ `sample-apps/storefront/storefront-7ff755c7dd-kpl8z`  
• *Fact:* The deployed checkout-gateway is currently a single replica with the image `docker.io/nvlannasik/checkout-gateway:latest` — potential bottleneck under downstream load — _Kubernetes deployments/readiness_ `sample-apps/Deployment/checkout-gateway`  
• *Fact:* The observed downstream timeout pattern aligns with the latency spike seen in the log trace, supporting a scaling/throughput issue rather than a purely code-path bug — _Loki_ + _Kubernetes_ combined view

[— Loki] {namespace="sample-apps", app="storefront"} | json | level = "error" — Loki logs
[— Kubernetes events] storefront readiness failures and readines probe failures — Kubernetes

*🚫 Ruled Out*
• No confirmed 5xx at the storefront API surface from Prometheus in this snapshot alone; the latency issue points to downstream dependency rather than an immediate storefront code-path fault. — Prometheus not definitive here
• A full outage of checkout-gateway is not observed; only a downstream timeout pattern is present. — pod/listings show gateway running

*📈 Confidence:* Medium — The evidence points to downstream timeouts in the checkout path and readiness instability, but exact endpoints, retry behavior, and precise load characteristics require a live runbook confirmation.

[OFFER] scale `sample-apps/Deployment/checkout-gateway` to 2 replicas

tools.name: k8s_cluster_health
tools.description: Pod health across the WHOLE cluster in one call: scans every namespace and returns only what is wrong (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled, Pending, not-ready) plus per-phase counts and how many pods/namespaces were actually scanned. USE THIS FIRST for any cluster-wide question — 'is anything broken', 'status check', 'cluster health', 'any pods down'. k8s_list_pods only sees ONE namespace, so answering those questions with it gives a partial answer that reads like a complete one. Pass namespace ONLY to narrow to a single namespace; omit it for the whole cluster. If scanned.complete is false the scan hit its ceiling — say so instead of reporting all-clear.

namespace.description: Optional — omit to scan the entire cluster (no default namespace)

restart_window_minutes.description: How recent a restart still counts as flapping for a now-ready pod (default: 60)

tools.name: k8s_correlate_pods
tools.description: Do several broken pods share ONE cause? Diffs the failing pods against the HEALTHY pods in the same namespace and returns what the broken set shares that no healthy pod has — node, image, ConfigMap, Secret, PVC, ServiceAccount, env variable names. USE THIS whenever more than one pod is failing, BEFORE investigating them one by one: k8s_describe_pod on each and comparing the specs yourself is what turns one shared root cause into eight separate write-ups. Omit `pods` to take every not-ready pod in the namespace (the natural follow-up to k8s_cluster_health). Read `uniqueToBroken` FIRST — `sharedWithHealthy` is mostly noise, because pods of one Deployment share nearly everything. An empty `uniqueToBroken` is a real answer: it says a single shared cause is unlikely, so look at the node, a recent deploy, or an upstream dependency instead. The output is a LEAD, never a conclusion — confirm the shared attribute with its own tool call before naming it as the root cause.

pods.description: Pod names to treat as broken (default: every not-ready pod in the namespace)

label_selector.description: Optional label selector to narrow which pods are considered at all

tools.name: k8s_list_namespaces
tools.description: List all namespaces in the Kubernetes cluster

tools.name: k8s_list_nodes
tools.description: List all nodes with status, roles, and resource capacity

tools.name: k8s_list_pods
tools.description: List pods in ONE namespace. For 'is anything broken across the cluster' use k8s_cluster_health instead — this tool cannot see past a single namespace

tools.name: k8s_get_pod_logs
tools.description: Get logs from a pod container. Set `previous: true` to read the CRASHED/prior container instance (the current logs are the fresh restart — CrashLoop root cause is in the previous one). `since_seconds` limits to a recent window.

previous.description: Logs from the previous (crashed) container instance (default: false)

container.description: Container name. Optional: on a pod with several containers (a sidecar, a proxy, a log shipper) omit it and the tool reads the one that is failing — restarted, or not ready — and names it and the others in the result, so you can ask for a different one by name.

since_seconds.description: Only logs from the last N seconds (optional)

tools.name: k8s_describe_pod
tools.description: Detailed status of ONE pod (the 'describe' view): per-container state incl. the exact termination/waiting reason (OOMKilled, exit code, CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff), restart counts, pod conditions, QoS, configured requests/limits, node. Use this for crash/OOM/not-Ready RCA — it gives the ground-truth reason logs only hint at. (No CPU/mem usage — that's Prometheus.) For a pod stuck Terminating it also returns `deletionTimestamp`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` and `finalizers` — those three decide the cause, and they are absent on a pod that is not being deleted.

tools.name: k8s_describe_node
tools.description: Detailed status of ONE node: conditions (Ready, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure), taints, unschedulable flag, capacity vs allocatable, kubelet/OS version. Use for Pending pods / node-level incidents. (No live usage — that's Prometheus.)

tools.name: k8s_get_endpoints
tools.description: Ready vs not-ready backend addresses (pods) behind a Service — answers 'does this Service have any ready endpoints?'. readyCount=0 explains 503 / connection-refused when the Service exists but has no healthy pods. Pass the Service name.

tools.name: k8s_list_deployments
tools.description: List deployments in a namespace, including each container's name and image (use this to answer image/tag questions)

tools.name: k8s_list_statefulsets
tools.description: List StatefulSets in a namespace, including each container's name and image

tools.name: k8s_list_daemonsets
tools.description: List DaemonSets in a namespace, including each container's name and image

tools.name: k8s_get_rollout_status
tools.description: Rollout progress of ONE Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet: desired vs updated/ready/available/unavailable replicas, `complete` flag, and conditions (e.g. Progressing=False ProgressDeadlineExceeded). Use for 'deploy stuck / not rolling out'.

tools.name: k8s_list_replicasets
tools.description: List ReplicaSets in a namespace with owner Deployment + revision + desired/ready + each container's image — rollout history (which RS is active vs stale, failed old RS). The image a rollback should go back to is the `images` entry of the newest older revision that still has ready pods: read it here rather than guessing a tag.

tools.name: k8s_list_pvs
tools.description: List PersistentVolumes (cluster-scoped): phase (Bound/Available/Released/Failed), capacity, storageClass, reclaimPolicy, bound claim — for storage incidents

tools.name: k8s_list_storageclasses
tools.description: List StorageClasses: provisioner, default flag, reclaim/binding mode — a PVC stuck Pending often means no default class or a broken provisioner

tools.name: k8s_list_network_policies
tools.description: List NetworkPolicies in a namespace: podSelector, policyTypes, rule counts — for 'traffic blocked' investigations (a deny-all policy or missing allow rule)

tools.name: k8s_list_pdbs
tools.description: List PodDisruptionBudgets in a namespace: min/maxUnavailable + disruptionsAllowed — disruptionsAllowed=0 blocks node drain/eviction and can stall rollouts

tools.name: k8s_get_sa_permissions
tools.description: What a ServiceAccount is allowed to do: its Role/ClusterRole bindings and the resolved rules (apiGroups/resources/verbs). Use for `forbidden` / permission-denied RCA — shows whether the SA is missing a needed permission.

tools.name: k8s_list_jobs
tools.description: List Jobs in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_cronjobs
tools.description: List CronJobs in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_services
tools.description: List Services in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_ingresses
tools.description: List Ingresses in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_hpas
tools.description: List HorizontalPodAutoscalers in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_pvcs
tools.description: List PersistentVolumeClaims in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_resource_quotas
tools.description: List ResourceQuotas in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_events
tools.description: List events in a namespace, optionally filtered by time

since_minutes.description: Only return events from the last N minutes (optional)

tools.name: k8s_list_crds
tools.description: List all CustomResourceDefinitions in the cluster (the types — use k8s_get_custom_resources for the objects)

tools.name: k8s_get_custom_resources
tools.description: Read custom resource OBJECTS of any CRD — e.g. Flux HelmRelease/Kustomization, cert-manager Certificate. Without `name`: compact list (name + Ready condition + message). With `name`: the full object (spec + status). Find group/version/plural via k8s_list_crds if unsure.

tools.name: k8s_find_by_name
tools.description: Find every object with this EXACT name across the kinds people name things by — Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, CronJob, Job, Pod, Service, Ingress, ConfigMap, Secret (name only), ServiceAccount, PersistentVolumeClaim — in one namespace or in all. Use it when you do not know what KIND a named object is, and before concluding that something does not exist: a lookup by a guessed kind comes back empty and reads exactly like absence. It says what a name IS, not whether it is unused — for a cleanup, k8s_find_unused_resources is still required. A name that is a namespace is reported as one. Each match carries its namespace and managedBy (flux / helm / none). Exact names only — it never suggests similar ones.

namespace.description: Namespace to search — omit to search every namespace

tools.name: k8s_get_resource
tools.description: Get ANY Kubernetes resource by apiVersion + kind — the full object (spec + status) when `name` is given, or a compact list when it's omitted. Works for built-ins (apiVersion `v1`, `apps/v1`, `batch/v1`, `networking.k8s.io/v1`, …) AND custom resources. Use when there's no dedicated tool for the kind, or you need the raw object. Discover which apiVersions this cluster serves via k8s_list_api_resources.

tools.name: k8s_list_api_resources
tools.description: Discover which API groups/versions this cluster serves (like `kubectl api-resources`/`api-versions`): core v1 kinds + every group with its versions. Use to find the right apiVersion for k8s_get_resource. For CRD types and their plurals use k8s_list_crds.

tools.description: List ServiceAccounts in a namespace

tools.name: k8s_list_configmaps
tools.description: List ConfigMaps in a namespace with their keys and data

tools.name: k8s_list_secrets
tools.description: List Secrets in a namespace (name and type only, values are not exposed)

tools.name: prometheus_list_metric_names

tools.name: alertmanager_get_alerts
tools.description: Get every alert Alertmanager is currently holding, in Alertmanager's own groups. This is the cluster-wide view of what is firing across ALL alert sources (Prometheus rules, log-based rules, anything else routed here) — use it to establish blast radius: is this incident isolated, or one symptom of something larger? Each alert is labelled with its status: active, silenced (a human muted the notification — the problem is still firing), or inhibited (suppressed by a higher-severity alert). Returns a summary with complete counts plus per-group detail.

filter.description: Optional label matchers, Alertmanager syntax, e.g. ['namespace="payments"'] or ['severity=~"critical|warning"']. Omit to see the whole cluster — which is what blast radius needs.

tools.name: tracing_search
tools.description: Search distributed traces (Tempo/Jaeger). Find slow or failing requests by service, minimum duration, and time window. Returns trace summaries — use tracing_get_trace for span detail.

end.description: Window end — RFC3339 or Unix seconds (default: now)

start.description: Window start — RFC3339 or Unix seconds (default: 1h ago)

service.description: Service name to filter by (REQUIRED for Jaeger backend, optional for Tempo)

minDurationMs.description: Only traces slower than this many milliseconds

tools.name: tracing_get_trace
tools.description: Get the full span tree for one trace by ID. Returns normalized spans (service, name, durationMs, parent, error) to pinpoint which span/service is slow or failing.

tools.name: tracing_list_services
tools.description: List service names known to the tracing backend (discovery before searching).

tools.name: k8s_find_unused_resources
tools.description: Orphaned/idle Kubernetes objects across the cluster in ONE call (the `kor` question): PVCs nothing mounts, Services with zero endpoint addresses, Deployments/StatefulSets scaled to 0, DaemonSets that match no node, and ConfigMaps/Secrets/ServiceAccounts nothing references. USE THIS for 'what can we clean up', 'unused resources', 'orphaned', 'idle', 'wasted', 'cost'. References are read from running pods AND every workload pod template, so a scaled-to-zero Deployment does NOT make its config look unused. Two more filters run on top: an object with an ownerReference is left out (its controller owns its lifecycle), and every surviving ConfigMap/Secret/PVC/ServiceAccount is cross-checked against EVERY custom resource in the cluster — so a ConfigMap an operator names in its CR spec is removed from the list, and `crossCheck.suppressed` says which CR saved it. ALWAYS read `crossCheck` and `note` before reporting: `crdsUnreadable` is non-empty when RBAC blocked some CRDs, and then the cross-check was PARTIAL — say so instead of calling the list verified. It stays a REVIEW list, not a delete list: an object read by name at runtime leaves no trace anywhere. Never propose deleting one without naming its owner. For sizing (requests/limits vs real usage) use k8s_recommend_resources instead — this tool reads no metrics.

namespace.description: Optional — omit to scan the whole cluster

cross_check_crds.description: Cross-check candidates against every custom resource in the cluster (default: true). Turn off only if the scan is too slow — the result is then unverified against operators

include_system_namespaces.description: Include kube-* namespaces (default: false — they are full of managed objects that only look unused)

tools.name: k8s_recommend_resources
tools.description: Right-sizing: compares each container's CONFIGURED requests/limits against its REAL usage from Prometheus and returns per-container recommendations plus the cluster's over-reserved CPU/memory. USE THIS for 'resource limits', 'requests', 'right-size', 'over-provisioned', 'how much does X actually use', and as the Short-term action in any OOMKilled / CPU-throttling / Pending-pod RCA — it produces the concrete number to change, so the recommendation is `512Mi -> 900Mi`, not 'consider raising the limit'. Flags: `oom_risk`, `cpu_throttled`, `cpu_under_provisioned`, `memory_under_provisioned`, `no_requests`, `over_provisioned`, `no_data`. Read `method` before quoting a number — it is a percentile heuristic over `window`, not a VPA verdict. Do NOT use it to find orphaned objects; that is k8s_find_unused_resources.

window.description: Lookback for the usage stats, e.g. 6h, 24h, 7d (default: 24h)

workload.description: Optional Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet name to narrow to

namespace.description: Optional — omit for every non-kube-* namespace

tools.name: k8s_rollout_restart
tools.description: [WRITE] Rolling-restart a Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet (kubectl rollout restart equivalent). Only works in namespaces listed in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. Call with dry_run=true first to validate the target without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

tools.name: k8s_set_image
tools.description: [WRITE] Change one container's image on a Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet (e.g. fix a nonexistent/broken image tag). Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates and reports current → new image without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

container.description: Container name within the pod template. Optional — omit for single-container workloads (auto-resolved)

tools.name: k8s_set_resources
tools.description: [WRITE] Update one container's resource requests/limits on a Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet (e.g. raise the memory limit after OOMKilled). Only provided values are changed. Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

container.description: Container name within the pod template. Optional — omit for single-container workloads (auto-resolved)

tools.name: k8s_scale
tools.description: [WRITE] Change the replica count of a Deployment/StatefulSet (DaemonSets have no replicas). Bounded by MAX_SCALE_DELTA. Scaling to zero is refused unless quarantine=true, which is only for a workload k8s_recommend_resources listed under idleWorkloads — a reversible alternative to deleting something that looks unused. Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

replicas.description: Target replica count (>= 1, or 0 with quarantine=true)

quarantine.description: Allow replicas=0 as a reversible quarantine of a workload measured idle over >=24h. Undo by scaling back to the original count. Never set this to retire a workload you have not measured.

tools.name: k8s_delete_pod
tools.description: [WRITE] Delete ONE stuck/wedged pod so its controller recreates it fresh (same spec). Refused for pods without a recreating controller (ReplicaSet/StatefulSet/DaemonSet) — no replacement = outage. GitOps-safe (like rollout_restart). Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates the target and reports the owning controller without changing anything.

pod.description: Exact pod name (not the workload name)

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

tools.name: k8s_delete_orphan
tools.description: [WRITE] Delete ONE abandoned object that nothing declares — a ConfigMap, Service, ServiceAccount, or a Deployment/StatefulSet already at 0 replicas. Only for objects k8s_find_unused_resources listed under `orphanKeys` (managedBy: none). REFUSED when anything declares it (Flux/Helm — remove it from the GitOps repo instead), when an ownerReference explains it, or when a workload still runs replicas. There is no minimum age on this server right now, so do not refuse one for being new — but state how old it is, because age is the only evidence of abandonment there is. Secrets and PersistentVolumeClaims are NOT supported and never will be: a Secret's backup is its credentials and a PVC's manifest is not its data. Returns `backupManifest` — the object as `kubectl apply` takes it back, captured immediately before deletion. That is the entire undo, so store it. Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true returns the manifest and every refusal without deleting anything.

kind.description: Object kind. No secret, no persistentvolumeclaim — neither can be restored from a manifest.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

tools.name: flux_reconcile
tools.description: [WRITE] Force Flux to re-apply the GitOps repo's declared state for a workload's HelmRelease (flux reconcile helmrelease --force equivalent), reverting changes made directly in the cluster. Use when the cluster has DRIFTED from Git (someone patched it outside GitOps) — it restores the declared state, it never introduces a new one. Refused for workloads not managed by a Flux HelmRelease. Only in ALLOWED_REMEDIATION_NAMESPACES. dry_run=true validates without changing anything.

dry_run.description: Server-side dry run: validate only, change nothing

answer.refused: the image being proposed is the image `checkout-gateway` is already running (`docker.io/nvlannasik/checkout-gateway:latest`), so this card would write the spec back to what it already says and change nothing. A rollout would restart the pods and they would come up on the same image, against the same fault. If the image really is the problem, the fix names a DIFFERENT tag — the one that was running before, or one the evidence shows works. If it is not the problem, say what is, or that the cause could not be determined.
